IN T HE COURT OF MR. SYED ALI JAWAD NAQVI , LEARNED CIVIL JUDGE, RAWALPINDI 
 
 
 
 
 Civil Suit No. 1919 / 20 26 
 
 
 
 Amjad Javeed 
 v ersus 
 M/s Mall 35 and others 
 
 
 (SUIT FOR RECOVERY OF RS. 1,344,000/- ALONG WITH INTEREST TILL REALIZATION OF THE AMOUNT AND DAMAGES ) 
 
 
 Application under Order IX Rule 7 read with section 151 Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for setting aside Order dated 1 9.02.2026 initiating ex-parte proceedings agains t the Applicant s /Defendant s No. 01 /Mall 35 
 
 Respectfully sheweth ; 
 That the titled sui t is pending adjudication before this learned Court, and is fixed for hearing on 08 -0 4 - 2026 . 
 That the Applicants / Defenda nt No. 01 is a Partnership Firm existing under the laws of Pakistan and ha s its registered office in Lahore (hereinafter referred to as Applicant /Defendant) . The Applicant is filing the instant Application through Syed Hassan Ali Shah , who is fully conversant with the facts of the case and has been duly authorized to file, sign and verify the pleadings to defend the titled Application . 
 
 ORDERS PASSED BY THE LEARNED COURT 
 That the learned Court passed the following Orders which subsequently lead to the ex parte proceedings: 
 Order dated 12 - 02 - 2026 
 T he titled suit was filed on 12-02-2026 and the learned Judge was pleased to Order that the Summons be sent to the Defenda nts “ through registered envelope AD /courier service … ” and the case was adjourned t o 19 - 0 2 - 2026 . 
 
 Order dated 19-02-2026 
 As per order dated 1 9-02-2026, Defendants proceeded ex-pa rte and case is adjourned for 04-03-2026 . 
 
 That through the instant Application, the Applicants seeks setting aside of ex-parte Order dated 19.02.2026 , as passed by th e learned Judge , and the consequent ex-parte proceedings, inter alia , on the following : 
 G R O U N D S 
 That the Applicants have never been served through all the necessary modes of service in accordance with law, more specifically, the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (“ CPC ”). This fact is evident from the record of this learned Court. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside. 
 
 That there is nothing on record to show that the Applicants had knowledge of the pending proceedings or the respective dates of hearings and consequently was avoiding service. That the record of the case is also silent in terms of any acknowledgement of the receipt of the registered communication or an endorsement by a courier messenger or postal employee that the Applicants refused to take delivery of summons, as envisaged in Order V Rule 10A, CPC . In fact, there is no record of any signature of any of Applicants ’s employees acknowledging the delivery of the said notices. Since the notices were never received by the Applicants , hence, it never got duly informed of filing of the titled suit . Therefore, the e x- p arte Order is liable to be set-aside/recalled on this score also. 
 
 That without prejudice to the averments made herein above, it may kindly be noted that the Plaintiff has failed to attach any evidence perta ining to the delivery of the AD courier sent to the Applicants ’s correct /actual address, as mentioned in the contracts/agreements signed by the plaintiff himself, nor any acknowledgment of such courier is available on the record. Therefore, Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set aside on this account also. 
 
 That only one mode of service was adopted before ex parte proceedings commenced against the Applicants . Under such circumstances, the learned Court could not have satisfied itself or ensured that the Applicants was avoiding service or had knowledge of the pending proceedings without first availing all modes of service that the Court has the authority to use under Order V, CPC. Hence, it is clear that the summons were not properly served on the Applicants , therefore , the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside/recalled. 
 That , apparently the process server of this learned Court never went to the actual address for the service of summons issued by this learned Court. Hence the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set-aside. 
 That this learned Court while passing the Ex-Parte Order against the Applicants did not consider the fact that summons/notices were neither witnessed by any person from the locality nor was any affidavit given in support of report therein. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order had been passed by this learned Court in contravention of mandatory provisions of law, which is not sustainable in the eye of law. 
 That it is trite law that suits should be properly adjudicat ed on merits instead of being knocked out on the basis of technicalities; therefore, given the fact that valuable legal rights of the Applicants are involved in the matter, it will be in the interest of justice that the ex-parte proceedings initiated through Order dated 19 - 0 2 - 2026 b e set-aside and the Applicants be given a fair opportunity of hearing and be allowed to defend itself in the titled suit . 
 That the stance of the Plaintiff , as stated in the plaint , is unfounded and the submissions of the Applicants or its respective stance before this learned Court through Written Statement and evidence in support there of, as well as the opportunity to challenge the version of the Plaintiff by subjecting the same to cross examination, are essential for fair and proper adjudication of the suit . 
 That even otherwise, it is the settled dictum of the Superior Courts of Pakistan that in the absence of any clear provisions in the CPC prohibiting the appearance and taking part in the proceedings by the defendant, there is no legal bar in allowing the defendant to defend its rights. It has been held in umpteen judicial precedents that the rules of procedure i.e. CPC, are meant to advance justice and preserve the rights of litigants and they are not to be interpreted in a way as to hamper the administration of justice. Hence, it is the right of the Applicants to take part in proceedings which have been proceeded ex-parte against it. 
 That from the averment s made herein a bove , it transpire s that ex-parte Order dated 19.02 .202 6 has been passed in a mechanical and hasty manner as mandatory requirements to effect service upon the Applicants have not been fulfilled and the Applicants has been deprived of it s lawful and legitimate right of defence . Hence, the said Ex-part e Order is liable to be set-aside /re-called. 
 That the Applicants come into kn owledge of the titled suit on last week , when the one of legal manager of the Applicants came to attend another case titled as ‘Shaikh Abdul Wahab Versus Mall 35 and other’ in the same court, hence the Application is well within the time. 
 That even otherwise, the right of fair trial is a fundamental right of every person, violation of which will lead to one inescapable conclusion, i.e. , destruction of the justice system. It is most respectfully submitted that any further proceedings in the instant matter shall be a direct violation of the said fundamental right of fair trial. Therefore, the Ex-Parte Order is liable to be set aside. 
 That it is trite law that no one should be condemned unheard. In the titled suit the golden principle of justice Audi alteram partem has severely compromised rendering the judicial process unsustainable. The Applicants has a valid undeniable right of being heard and treated as per law. 
 That the Applicants very respectfully seeks leave to raise addition al grounds at the bar. 
 PRAYER: 
 In the circumstances, it is respectfully prayed that the instant Application may kindly be accepted, and ex-parte Order dated 19 . 0 2 . 202 6 along with subsequent ex-parte proceedings conducted in the titled suit may graciously be set aside and the Applicants may be allowed to join the proceedings in the titled suit . 
 Any other relief which this learned Court may deem fit in favour of the Applicants may also graciously be awarded.
